subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
subtype: Approach: talking to the manager about flexible hours [Action]
passage: I had rehearsed it three times before I knocked on Siddharth's door. My father had come home from hospital, and I could no longer do his mornings and still be at my desk by nine. I did not ask for sympathy. I brought a page. I would work from home on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and on those days I would send Siddharth a short note by noon saying what I planned to finish, and another at six saying what I had. My reports would be on time and my calls covered. Siddharth read it twice and asked two questions, about the Thursday client call and about who to contact when I was offline. Then Siddharth said yes, for a three-month trial. I walked back to my desk shaky with relief. - Darshan

qa.q: On which days did Darshan propose working from home?
How did Darshan feel after Siddharth agreed?
qa.a: Darshan felt relieved, though still shaky from nerves.

qa.q: What could Darshan do to keep the arrangement going after the trial?
qa.a: Darshan could keep sending the promised notes on time and review the results at the end of the trial, since reliable output builds trust.

qa.q: How might Siddharth have seen the proposal?
qa.a: Siddharth may have valued that it came with clear outputs and a way to reach Darshan, which made it easy to say yes.

grounding: Darshan brings a clear proposal to work from home two days a week with defined output and it is accepted.
